# MiniDev UI

> 548 free, MIT-licensed React + Tailwind v4 components for product UI: forms, data tables, charts, billing, auth, settings, overlays, and AI surfaces (chat, reasoning, tool calls). Built on Base UI. Hairline design language: 1px structure, semantic OKLCH tokens, light + dark from one token set.

## Install

- npm: `npm i minidev-ui-kit` then `import { Button } from "minidev-ui-kit/ui/button"` (Next.js: add `transpilePackages: ["minidev-ui-kit"]`)
- shadcn CLI, one file at a time: `npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.minidev.pro/r/<name>.json`
- Or copy the single source file into your repo. Every component is one file.

## Rules for generating code with MiniDev UI

- Use semantic tokens only: bg, surface, raised, sunken, border, border-strong, fg, fg-muted, fg-subtle, ink, on-ink, accent, accent-soft, accent-fg, success, warning, danger, info. Never raw hex or palette steps like blue-500.
- Primary actions use <Button> (ink). Brand-coloured actions use <Button variant="accent">. Secondary: variant="outline". Quiet: variant="ghost".
- Depth: shadow-xs, shadow-sm, shadow-raised (cards), shadow-md, shadow-lg, shadow-overlay (menus, dialogs). No other shadows.
- Radius: controls rounded-lg (8px), cards rounded-xl (12px), overlays rounded-2xl. Nested radius = outer minus padding.
- Numbers are tabular (tabular-nums). Headings use negative tracking; body text does not.
- Dark mode: add the `dark` class to <html>. Components never branch on theme.

- [Build a billing page in Next.js with Stripe](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/nextjs-billing-page-stripe): Build a SaaS billing page in Next.js with Stripe: plans, usage, invoices, payment methods and cancellation, loaded on the server and kept in sync by webhooks.

- [Build a React data table with TanStack Table and Tailwind](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/react-data-table-tanstack): Build a React data table with TanStack Table v8 and Tailwind: sorting, search, filters, pagination, row selection, bulk actions and column visibility.
- [Date range picker in React with presets, two months and keyboard](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/react-date-range-picker): Build a React date range picker with Tailwind: native date inputs first, then a two month calendar in a popover with presets, arrow keys and ISO string values.

- [File upload in React: dropzone, progress and previews](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/react-file-upload-dropzone): Build file upload in React with a drag and drop dropzone, accept rules, real upload progress, presigned S3 URLs, cancel and retry, and image previews.

- [Product tour and feature spotlight in React](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/react-product-tour): Build a product tour in React: a spotlight cutout over real UI, a popover anchored to each target, step state, keyboard support and a seen flag.

- [Design a SaaS settings page that scales](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/saas-settings-page): Design a SaaS settings page in React that scales: information architecture, autosave vs explicit save, team roles, API keys and safe destructive actions.
- [How to install components from a custom shadcn registry](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/shadcn-custom-registry): Install shadcn components from any registry URL: what the item JSON contains, how registryDependencies resolve, components.json setup and common fixes.
- [Build a collapsible sidebar layout for a SaaS app](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/shadcn-sidebar-layout): Build a collapsible React sidebar layout in Next.js: active links with usePathname, a Cmd+B shortcut, collapsed state saved in a cookie and a mobile drawer.
- [Hero section patterns in React and Tailwind: 8 layouts that convert](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/tailwind-hero-section-examples): Eight hero section layouts for React and Tailwind v4, each with the props it takes, what it is good for, and how to keep it fast and accessible above the fold.
- [Migrating a component library to Tailwind CSS v4](https://ui.minidev.pro/guides/tailwind-v4-migration): Migrate a component library to Tailwind CSS v4: CSS-first config with @theme, the upgrade tool, renamed utilities, border and ring defaults, and OKLCH tokens.

## Glossary

- [:focus-visible](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/focus-visible): :focus-visible is a CSS pseudo-class that matches a focused element only when the browser decides focus should be shown, typically during keyboard use.
- [Accordion](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/accordion): An accordion is a vertical stack of headings that each expand or collapse a section of content, so users reveal only the parts they need.
- [ARIA](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/aria): ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) is a W3C set of HTML attributes that tells assistive technology what custom UI elements are and their state.
- [Avatar](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/avatar): An avatar is a small image, usually round, that represents a person, team or organization, with initials or an icon shown when no image is available.
- [backdrop-filter (CSS)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/backdrop-filter): backdrop-filter is a CSS property that applies filters such as blur or saturate to whatever is rendered behind an element, the basis of frosted glass UI.
- [Badge](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/badge): A badge is a small, non-interactive label attached to another element that shows a status, a category or a count, such as Paid, Beta or 3 unread.
- [Banner](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/banner): A banner is a persistent message bar across the top of a page or section that stays visible until the situation it describes changes or the user dismisses it.
- [Base UI](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/base-ui): Base UI is an open source library of unstyled, accessible React components from the team behind Radix, Floating UI and Material UI.
- [Bento grid](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/bento-grid): A bento grid is a layout of rectangular tiles in different sizes on one shared grid, used to show several features or stats at once, like a bento box.
- [Breadcrumbs](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/breadcrumbs): Breadcrumbs are a row of links showing where the current page sits in a site's hierarchy, letting users jump back to any parent level.
- [Card](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/card): A card is a bordered or shadowed container that groups a related set of content and actions into one unit, such as a product, a stat or a post.
- [clamp() (CSS)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/clamp): The CSS clamp() function picks a value between a minimum and a maximum from a preferred value in between, so one expression replaces several media queries.
- [color-mix()](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/color-mix): The CSS color-mix() function blends two colors by percentage in a chosen color space, for example an accent mixed with transparent to tint it from one token.
- [Combobox](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/combobox): A combobox is an input paired with a popup list of options, where typing filters the list and the user picks a value with the mouse or keyboard.
- [Command palette](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/command-palette): A command palette is a searchable modal, usually opened with Cmd+K or Ctrl+K, that lets users run actions and jump to pages by typing.
- [Component library](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/component-library): A component library is a collection of reusable, tested UI components, such as buttons, inputs and dialogs, that teams assemble interfaces from.
- [Compound components](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/compound-components): Compound components are a set of React components, like Tabs, TabsList and TabsTrigger, that share state through context and are composed together in JSX.
- [Container queries](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/container-queries): Container queries let CSS style an element based on the size of its parent container rather than the viewport, so a card adapts to the column it sits in.
- [Controlled component](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/controlled-component): A controlled component is a React input whose value is held in state and passed down as a prop, with onChange reporting edits, so state is the source of truth.
- [CSS variables (custom properties)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/css-variables): CSS variables, or custom properties, are author-defined properties named with two leading dashes whose values you reuse with var() and that inherit.
- [Dark mode](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/dark-mode): Dark mode is a color scheme that renders light text on dark surfaces, chosen by the user or taken from the operating system's preference.
- [Data table](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/data-table): A data table is an interactive grid of records with columns you can sort, filter, paginate and select, built for scanning and acting on structured data.
- [Date range picker](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/date-range-picker): A date range picker is a form control for choosing a start date and an end date together, usually with a calendar and presets like Last 30 days.
- [Debounce](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/debounce): Debouncing delays a function until its trigger has been quiet for a set time, so a search box sends one request after typing stops, not one per keystroke.
- [Design system](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/design-system): A design system is the shared set of principles, tokens, components and guidelines a team uses to build consistent products at scale.
- [Design tokens](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/design-tokens): Design tokens are named, platform-agnostic values for design decisions such as colors, spacing, type and shadows, shared between design and code.
- [Drawer](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/drawer): A drawer is a panel that slides in from an edge of the screen over the page, used for navigation, filters or quick actions, and slides back when dismissed.
- [Dropdown menu](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/dropdown-menu): A dropdown menu is a list of actions or options that opens below a button, where arrow keys move through the items and Enter runs the chosen one.
- [Empty state](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/empty-state): An empty state is what a screen shows when there is no data to display yet, explaining why it is empty and offering the next useful action.
- [Fluid typography](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/fluid-typography): Fluid typography sizes text with clamp() and viewport or container units so it scales smoothly between a minimum and a maximum with no breakpoint jumps.
- [Focus trap](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/focus-trap): A focus trap keeps keyboard focus inside an open modal, so Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through its controls instead of escaping to the page behind it.
- [FOUC (flash of unstyled content)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/fouc): FOUC (flash of unstyled content) is when a browser briefly paints a page before its styles apply, so users see raw or wrong-looking content flicker.
- [Glassmorphism](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/glassmorphism): Glassmorphism is a UI style that draws panels as frosted glass: a translucent fill, a background blur from backdrop-filter, and a thin light edge.
- [Headless components](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/headless-components): Headless components provide behavior, state and accessibility for UI widgets without any styles, so you supply all of the visual design yourself.
- [Hero section](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/hero-section): A hero section is the first full-width block of a landing page, stating what the product does and offering one primary action above the fold.
- [Hydration (React)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/hydration): Hydration is the process where React attaches event handlers and state to HTML rendered on the server, making the static markup interactive.
- [Infinite scroll](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/infinite-scroll): Infinite scroll loads the next batch of content automatically as the user nears the end of a list, instead of asking them to click to another page.
- [Kanban board](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/kanban-board): A kanban board shows work items as cards in columns that represent stages, so moving a card to another column changes its status.
- [Live region (aria-live)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/live-region): A live region is an element marked with aria-live or role=\"status\" whose content changes are announced by screen readers without moving focus to it.
- [Loading spinner](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/loading-spinner): A loading spinner is a small rotating indicator that shows work is in progress when the duration is unknown, used inside buttons and for short waits.
- [Logical properties](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/logical-properties): Logical properties are CSS properties defined relative to writing direction, like margin-inline-start rather than margin-left, so layouts mirror in RTL.
- [Micro-interactions](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/micro-interactions): Micro-interactions are small, single-purpose moments of feedback, like a toggle sliding or a copy icon becoming a check, that confirm what just happened.
- [Modal dialog](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/modal-dialog): A modal dialog is a window layered over the page that blocks interaction with everything behind it until the user completes or dismisses it.
- [Multi-select](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/multi-select): A multi-select is a form control that lets users pick several options from one list, showing the chosen items as check marks or removable chips.
- [Neumorphism](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/neumorphism): Neumorphism is a soft UI style where elements look extruded from or pressed into the background, using paired light and dark shadows on one color.
- [OKLCH](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/oklch): OKLCH is a CSS color space that describes colors by perceptual lightness, chroma and hue, so equal numeric steps look like equal visual steps.
- [Optimistic UI](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/optimistic-ui): Optimistic UI updates the interface immediately as if an action succeeded, then syncs with the server and rolls back if the request fails.
- [Pagination](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/pagination): Pagination splits a long set of results into numbered pages with controls to move between them, so each view loads a fixed, predictable amount.
- [Polymorphic component (asChild and render)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/polymorphic-component): A polymorphic component can render as a different element or component than its default, so a Button can be a link while keeping its styles and behavior.
- [Popover](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/popover): A popover is a small floating panel anchored to the control that opened it, holding rich or interactive content, that closes on Escape or a click outside.
- [Portal](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/portal): A portal renders part of a React tree into a different DOM node, usually document.body, so dialogs and popovers escape overflow clipping and stacking contexts.
- [prefers-reduced-motion](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/prefers-reduced-motion): prefers-reduced-motion is a CSS media feature that reports whether the user has asked the operating system to minimize nonessential animation.
- [Progress bar](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/progress-bar): A progress bar is a horizontal track that fills to show how much of a task is done, as a measured percentage or an indeterminate animation when unknown.
- [Radio group](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/radio-group): A radio group is a set of options where selecting one deselects the rest, used when a form needs exactly one choice from a short, visible list.
- [Radix UI](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/radix-ui): Radix UI is an open source library of unstyled, accessible React primitives, widely known as the original foundation of shadcn/ui.
- [Range slider](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/range-slider): A range slider is a slider with two thumbs on one track that sets a minimum and a maximum together, such as a price range on a filter panel.
- [React Server Components](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/react-server-components): React Server Components render only on the server and send their output, not their code, to the browser, which cuts the JavaScript users download.
- [Render props](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/render-props): A render prop is a prop whose value is a function returning React elements, letting a component hand data or state to the caller, who decides the markup.
- [Roving tabindex](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/roving-tabindex): Roving tabindex is a keyboard pattern where a group of controls shares one Tab stop and arrow keys move focus inside it; only the active item has tabindex 0.
- [Scroll snap](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/scroll-snap): CSS scroll snap makes a scroll container stop at defined points, such as the start of each slide, so carousels and galleries land cleanly without JavaScript.
- [Segmented control](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/segmented-control): A segmented control is a row of two to five connected buttons where exactly one is selected, used to switch a view, a mode or a value in place.
- [Semantic tokens](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/semantic-tokens): Semantic tokens are design tokens named for their purpose, such as fg-muted or danger, rather than their value, so themes can change values safely.
- [shadcn registry](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/shadcn-registry): A shadcn registry is a set of JSON files describing components and their dependencies that the shadcn CLI can install directly into a project.
- [shadcn/ui](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/shadcn-ui): shadcn/ui is an open source collection of React and Tailwind CSS components that you copy into your project with a CLI instead of installing a package.
- [Side sheet](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/side-sheet): A side sheet is a panel that slides in from the left or right edge to show details or a form beside the main content, either over it or pushing it aside.
- [Skeleton screen](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/skeleton-screen): A skeleton screen is a placeholder layout of gray shapes that mirrors a page's structure while its content loads, instead of a blank screen or spinner.
- [Skip link](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/skip-link): A skip link is a hidden link at the top of a page that appears on keyboard focus and jumps straight to the main content, bypassing the header and navigation.
- [Snackbar](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/snackbar): A snackbar is a brief message bar at the bottom of the screen that confirms an action and can offer one follow-up, such as Undo, before it disappears.
- [Split-flap display](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/split-flap-display): A split-flap display shows characters on hinged flaps that flip in sequence to change, like a train station departure board, often recreated in CSS.
- [Stepper (multi-step form)](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/stepper): A stepper splits a long form or process into ordered steps and shows progress through them, with one step's fields visible at a time.
- [Tabs](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/tabs): Tabs are a row of labeled triggers that switch between panels of content in the same place, showing one panel at a time without leaving the page.
- [Tailwind CSS v4](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/tailwind-css-v4): Tailwind CSS v4 is the fourth major version of the utility-first CSS framework, with a faster engine and configuration written in CSS instead of JavaScript.
- [Throttle](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/throttle): Throttling limits how often a function can run, to at most once per interval, so a scroll or pointer handler fires on a steady schedule, not on every event.
- [Timeline](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/timeline): A timeline is a vertical list of events in time order, each with a marker on a shared line, a timestamp and a short description, as in an activity feed.
- [Toast notification](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/toast-notification): A toast is a brief, non-modal message that appears at the edge of the screen to confirm an action or report status, then dismisses itself.
- [Toggle switch](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/toggle-switch): A toggle switch is an on-off control with a sliding thumb that applies a setting immediately, like a physical light switch, without a Save button.
- [Tooltip](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/tooltip): A tooltip is a small text label that appears when a control is hovered or focused, describing it briefly without taking space in the layout.
- [Tree view](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/tree-view): A tree view is a nested list of expandable nodes, like a file explorer, where each branch can be opened to reveal its children and collapsed to hide them.
- [View Transitions API](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/view-transitions): The View Transitions API animates between two states of a page by snapshotting the old view, applying the change and crossfading or morphing to the new one.
- [Virtual scrolling](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/virtual-scrolling): Virtual scrolling renders only the rows of a long list that are visible in the viewport, plus a small buffer, so a list of 100,000 items stays fast.
- [Visually hidden](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/visually-hidden): Visually hidden is a CSS technique that removes an element from view while keeping it in the accessibility tree, so screen readers still read its text.
- [WCAG color contrast](https://ui.minidev.pro/glossary/wcag-contrast): WCAG color contrast is the minimum luminance ratio between text or UI and its background: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI parts at AA.
